newsitem.title: FRANCE: Accor, Carlson speed up travel merger.
newsitem.headline: Accor, Carlson speed up travel merger.

text.p: French hotels and travel group Accor and Carlson Companies Inc of the U.S. have decided to speed up the planned merger of their business travel activities into Carlson Wagonlit Travel, an Accor spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

Earlier Accor had sent invitations for a January 31 news conference by its management chairman Jean-Marc Espallioux, Carlson's Marilyn Carlson-Nelson and Jean-Marc Simon after the signing of a merger agreement.
"We first decided to work together in 1994 and at the time we planned to merge in five years' time. We have now decided to speed this up," the spokeswoman said.
She declined to give any further information ahead of the news conference.
Earlier this month, Travis Tanner was made global president and chief executive officer of Carlson Wagonlit Travel, to be based at the Miami, Florida, headquarters.
He will have three world region presidents reporting to him.

Paris-based Accor and Minneapolis-based Carlson set up Carlson Wagonlit as a 50/50 joint venture in March 1994, creating a world rank company with 4,000 travel agencies in 125 countries and sales of over $10 billion.

Espallioux, a former finance director at Generale des Eaux, was named chairman of Accor in October 1996, taking over from Paul Dubrule and Gerard Pelisson who remain chairmen of the supervisory board.
